comparator.sourceNotes: The programme-specific Appendix I 2026–2027, printed pages 55–59 and cohort 9A201-2026, supplies the ordinary English full-time Tilburg sequence: 60 EC in each of three years. Every named course is represented separately; the third-year 30-EC mobility/minor window remains genuine open space. Old Testament: Torah and Prophetic Literature (U20074-B-6) carries 6 EC in the formal cohort table, correcting the general webpage's 3-EC display; there is no missing three-credit unit. Research and academic skills (12 EC) are embedded in named course weights and are not additional credit. Yellow-coded compulsory units rotate every two years and appear once in the specified cohort sequence. Ordinary Hebrew, Greek and Latin requirements are retained; Greek exemptions and replacement of Latin for an intended teacher-training master require the stated conditions/Board permission and are alternatives, not extra components. The merged registry target covers English Tilburg and Dutch Utrecht delivery plus part-time pacing. English full-time is an ordinary representative delivery, not an English-only target inferred from its translated name. The public reader was recorded as published on 14 September 2026; its general body retains a stale 2025–2026 effective-date clause, so the explicitly dated 2026 cohort appendix controls this reconstruction. Appendix and external allocation checked 2026-10-08; the external allocation and source conflict were rechecked on 2026-10-14; the settled comparator remains unchanged while the UCR judgment is independently reassessed.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target combines ordinary English Tilburg and Dutch Utrecht deliveries and full-/part-time modes. The ordinary English full-time Tilburg delivery provides an explicitly dated September 2026 cohort sequence for the same broad Theology bachelor, without selecting a shortened prior-degree pathway or the optional canonical-degree package. Translation of the registry display name does not establish an exclusive English target; delivery choice is independent of UCR fit.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

Historical, literary and cultural interpretation of traditions, texts, myths and religious heritage
Social-scientific study of religion, identity, institutions, lived belief and public life

How should people and institutions reason about justice, tolerance and responsibility in complex societies?

alternatives.label: Belief, worldviews, cultural traditions & public life
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is weighted toward philosophy, histories and narratives of belief, cultural heritage, social analysis and religion’s public context. It does not claim scripture, source languages, dogmatics, liturgy or pastoral theology.
alternatives.concept: Study belief, meaning, worldviews and identity through philosophy, literature, myth, history, heritage, sociology, psychology, law and politics. This is the strongest bounded religion-and-worldviews response, not a Theology degree.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Year-1 PPD and seven level-300 courses. Law, Society & Justice precedes Comparative Constitutional Law; the remaining selected courses have no formal prerequisites, and all are offered in their assigned Fall-2026-cohort terms.

alternatives.label: Ethics, justice & social responsibility
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates on ethical theory, human rights, law, political philosophy, sociology, public institutions, conflict and environmental justice, matching the target’s explicit justice, tolerance and responsibility questions.
alternatives.concept: Study moral reasoning, rights, justice, legal and political institutions, social theory, conflict and public responsibility in plural societies. This is a secular ethics-and-public-life route grounded in target evidence, not Catholic applied ethics or theology.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with Alternative 1, this route replaces twelve literature, heritage, media, psychology and belief-history courses with twelve courses in human rights, criminal, international, private and EU law, political institutions, modern sociology, social movements, advanced ethics and public communication (90 EC unique on each side).
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Year-1 PPD and eight level-300 courses. Law, Society & Justice precedes every dependent law course; all other courses have no formal prerequisites, and each is placed in an exact term shown in the authoritative workbook.

blocks: Both engage the history of philosophy; UCR provides a broad Western-philosophy survey rather than theology’s integrated philosophical sequence.
Both develop ethical reasoning and character; UCR is non-confessional moral philosophy rather than theology-specific ethics.
Disciplinary requirements not reproduced at UCR

selection.assessment: The historical exception treated the absence of a full Theology discipline as dispositive. A bounded religion-and-worldviews closest response is coherent, and the target’s explicit justice, tolerance and responsibility questions support a materially different ethics-and-public-life route. The stable education minor was then assessed, but UCR has no coherent pedagogy, curriculum-design, supervised-school-practice or teacher-qualification sequence with which to construct a third 24-course programme. No further generator-eligible direction remains.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes are bounded related-field responses. They study belief, worldviews, meaning, ethics, justice and religion in cultural and public life, but do not reproduce Tilburg’s Catholic-theology identity, biblical source languages, exegesis, dogmatics, systematic and practical theology, liturgy, canon law, patristics or Theology thesis.

The public programme page still displays Old Testament: Torah and Prophetic Literature as 3 EC, while the adopted September 2026 cohort appendix gives U20074-B-6 as 6 EC. The formal 6-EC value remains controlling; the complete 180-EC comparator and neutral English full-time Tilburg route are preserved unchanged.
